content: "the gods and these wardens will make their own place no matter what we decide that's what they do. say something else or get out."
"And yet there's still more to fear. Greed, abuse, a lack of compassion. I seek a system that guards against those fears that came in with us."
Vivica nods to Bones
She is tired of talking about gods and wardens
Cascadia departs shaking her head.
"A system that works with power granted by higher beings would work." The speaker says as he peruses the midaskian document once more.

"there will be many who will look to the wardens and the gods for their choices. but going in circles abiut them isn't what we're here for. we're about trying to jot down what we are building and why it would help people. Not repeatedly spouting over what we think is best with no solid ground."
"Draft a system then. You argue and argue about how they are needed. Draft how it would work because right now I can only see it as something I cannot agree with."
Vivica will hand <@339235123759153162> a copy of the drafted constitution (its pinned)
"Drafting a system is what we're already doing here. You draft with the written word and I draft with spoken debate."

The fey man has been reading over the proposal for some time, and eventually looks up. "This seems... broadly acceptable." He turns to Vivica "though there are a number of things that should be clarified. I believe I understand the sentiment behind many of the sections, but with no definition a government would be unable to ratify such a constitution with so many different interpretations. I would greatly appreciate explanations of many of the concepts herein, such as 'restorative justice' and the like." (Please do not rush on this, I know y'all have spent a long ass time working on it and deserve a break)
The raven nods. "Alright. Bones is right. Helping people. At the end of the day, we should build a society that helps people, and encourages us to help each other."
"I'll write up a clearer explanation of this system for those who are unfamiliar with it." She nods
"Back to the housing thing... who will be providing the housing? If workers will earn a livable wage, enough for them to own their own living space, where will that come from?"
Vivica gets down to writing (and with that I've found my out to take a break ✌)
Malathor's lips curl into a small smile. "I *love democracy.*"

"What about the in-between beings. Those... Who share this place with fey wood that have their own kingdom. Or the city of angels who rule themselves and follow laws that are unknowable because they are unspeakable by mortal mouthes. Will those that are here retain their rights even if they hold customs that  run counter to this new government."
"I am only a person with an opinion but I would preach for a certain level of tolerance."
The white leonin who spoke nods.

In a burst of light, Lucy vanishes.
(Gotta get some sleep myself)

"if they are foreign and from some otherworld they are foreign. they should be treated courteously in their business but it would be easier to respect them as foreign. respect what we do on this side, if it's about dealings in their own laws then they have a right to work with local jurisdiction to sort it out."
"perhaps we should make a clause about deals with otherworld folk."
"The ruling faction in the city of angels takes the letter of the law very seriously. This ought to be addressed."
"Speaking of language, I expect we might keep both Common and Arcanian as our national languages?"
"it'd be fair to the locals."

"And should it pass that public education is a right, what's the method of teaching? I was taught to speak in Elvish when I was young. I value the differences, and that we all still can speak with each other, but I'm thinking about this."

** **
"*Language is the weapon minds use to defy the tyranny of time,*" Irynx quotes. "It would make sense for us to unite with it."
"there's two pitfalls. language confusion dividing, or language stripping individuals of heritage. not everyone is skilled at picking them up."
Mictlan tilts their head, slightly. "I would. Agree. That languages. Are difficult. There could maybe be. Schools. Set up. For different. Cultures."
"Languages at home with the people of our heritage, and languages at school for the people of our nation."
"would make resources thin. but often people can have a mother tongue of their heritage, and a tongue of the country they live in. the mother tongue is responsibility of the family."
(pretty much what irynx said)
"What about. The somewhat young who. Come. With no knowledge. Of the languages here. Would they be. Expected. To learn Common. Through miming."
"lots of magic can take care of it. but there should be a right to translation."
"A right to be understood," she nods.
"right to effective communication for those picky." looking to the leonin
Mictlan hums. "That is. Somewhat. Acceptable."
They look down at their notes. "Speaking of. How will. Citizenship. Be defined."

"I'm sure there's gonna be some legalese there and I'm bad at that so I'm not at liberty to say. My answer — and again, not the only voice in the room here, you're all allowed to stop me and say your own thing — is if someone wants to be a part of Arcania, they must be in all sense of the word."

Vivica looks up from her notes "Do we even need a national language? What if we just sent the standard that we print official documents in multiple languages? Say the 5 most common or something. It would make communication between the state and the people pretty effective and also allows people to favor their native tongue." She says while consolidating her notes
"Less about the documents and more the method of teaching, for public education."

"Knowing multiple languages will be good for kids, good for the brain. I think I learned my 3rd language by the time I was  34. I know about 6 now. I definitely support multiple languages in education, its been a life saver."
"However I think a lot of these choices will be better decided by the people in their communities and the senate if they choose to make laws about it."
Finn finishes discussing the finer points of his proposal with members of the continental congress before returning back over
"Well, that went well. No specks of blood and everyone has their toes!"
Vivica smiles at him "I've been passing out copies to some of our people. Hopefully we'll be well received. "

"It seems a lot of people like getting bogged down with specific legislation rather than addressing the Midaskian system of government. 

Electing leaders, checks and balances, and legislation being created through the system we put in place. It's like some people think of this as a town charter of a settlement that needs all its laws written out rather than just a system of government that can functionally pass laws. "
Vivica nods "I agree fully. There is a lot of conversation regarding things that take place after the form of government has been decided on."

"It seems a little too detached for my liking." Speaks a small sprite carrying what appears to be a toothpick. "It seems ridiculous to even try and have a government that big. Even in this city alone we've got five different Burroughs, assuming you counts the island completely controlled by the reds. Even those five trying to work together has proven tricky in the past. I could see bringing together a few cities and communities, but multiple states? I'd prefer we just build a military alliance with rules then allow it to disband after we get rid of the British." The sprite's voice is small yet commanding, and speaks with authority.

"A valid point. Introducing a system of divisions might prove to be harmful against our cause. It will be difficult to organize different states and conflicts of interest among them will threaten our nation's unity. But I do not agree with the idea of a military alliance, rather a strong central authority should govern us. The central authority's influence can be spread throughout the nation by means of magic and technology. There is no need for divisions, unity is what we need to remain steadfast."

"And continuing on the concept of unity. The three branches you are proposing, judiciary, legislative, and executive, need not be seperated. The judiciary's responsibilities can be handled by magics. Such magics like the zone of truth you have written here would work but we can go further with charm spells to truly wring out the truth. And the priestess' spear of Gungir, a geas spell, and other magics can also exact oaths from someone. The legislative and executive can be handled by one body, the central authority I was speaking for example. Checks and balances doesn't need to be internally set-up. Balance between the authority and the governed could be done instead. As per Mender's words, 'A well placed sword is the check.' Instead of a competition amongs the branches of government we should implement a system where the ruling authority should maintain the confidence and trust of its governed, not it's peers in office."
"And the idea of higher beings keeping our leaders in check is still something I would want to be kept on the table."
"If we consider the collective people of Arcania as a high power. Alongside wardens and aspects and gods, we should get to keep our leaders in check too."
The speaker nods. "There is no need for internal checks and balances."

"But this requires we know what's going on. There aren't any truly omniscient beings. Even Odin used the ravens to keep his eye on the world. We should know what goes on in the room where it happens, as boring as it is sometimes."
An elven woman with red hair nods and speaks in a slight Irish accent. "Let those in power do their job, everyone else's is to make sure they do it well."
(Irynx, your recognize this woman as Fiona Kelly.)
"The central authority should be transparent in whatever they do. The people deserve to know."

"But how would we know where to draw the line between what we can and can't see? Officials deserve a right to privacy, moreso than the average citizen given so much of their life is public." Speaks up an elven man next to the redhead who is holding her hand. "Maybe a group of qualified individuals who have no other job than to ensure those in power do their job? I know I'd be much more comfortable performing that kind of public service than proper legislation? Maybe a council of concerned citizens?"

The raven nods again. "Officials deserve privacy in matters that don't concern the rest of us. I don't want to see them bathing but I do want to know if they're planning on starting a war or something."

"Official deserve a right to privacy in their personal lives, that much is sure. But in matters of state, they should let us know everything. We live and work for this country, and we ought to know what is happening with it."
"Even if they happen to be making war plans in the bath." She adds.
"Of course, but can we stop them from taking about matters of state while in the bath?" Asks the man.
"Exactly!" He says, looking to irynx
"Them being in the bath is not the point. As regular people, they are free to hold secrets. But as leaders they should inform the governed of every issue and decision they face."
His mouth twitches slightly seeing Irynx but makes no obvious sign of disgust or anything.
(bird or not, guess he knows 😔 )
"I don't know about the council of concerned citizens, though. Maybe if they were sworn to keep the public in the know, rather than keep the power in check? Hm. Thinking."
(he might just not like birds)

A treaty has been offered, should finn's constitution be ratified.

"Excuse me fellow citizen, is that is what you are." Says Ryan Kelly, walking over to bird Irynx. "My name is Ryan Kelly. Some of my friends and I were wondering if you have a more humanoid form? We find out somewhat distracting and hard to engage in conversation with an... animal."

"Having the Warden's help during times of crisis would be a massive boon. Let us consider integrating them in our nation. They are the ones protecting us from the perils of the old world, they are powerful allies."

Roy walks over to Irynx and changes to his shifter form.
"Is there a *problem*, good *sir*? Surely you're not going to think less of people just because they don't look the way you'd like? After all you've joined this congress to debate about the good of *all people* of Arcania, like a good fellow citizen, isn't that right?"

"I'm sure others found it very amusing, actually. I will consider your comfort, but at the end of the day, it's my body. Probably one of those private matters we were talking about, not a concern of the public."

(heck it I'm in)
a slightly pale, slightly dripping frog - Sabrine walks in, nodding to Roy and the spider-form Kukudh chilling with the swarm. she takes the stand. 'Arcania needs to be a place of freedom for everyone. Not just the majority. We need to accommodate all people.'
'Everyone should be able to get the help they need, whether physically, socially, mentally, or anything else.'

Finn reads over the proposed Treaty of the Wardens carefully and with excitement

"If this gets ratified and discussed with them, I'm sure we could create a great treaty with the natural forces of Arcania. I think this affirms that we keep out religious entities from forming fundamental pieces of the government in cases where they may not be there forever. This could have us live in great harmony with the land we call home"
Vivica reads through the treaty. "I like this a lot. It could become a great foundation for a positive relationship with the residents of this land."
'Everyone deserves to be able to live as who they are, without fear of retribution or abandonment.' she looks around the room, her gaze lingering on Ryan and Fiona for a second.

"Also on the topic of privacy for officials and the government. This constitutional proposal has several aspects where transparency is a pillar of its design and for records. It compliments the lamplighters records and ravens of memories, but does not rely or cater to them specifically"
"Also, Speaker, the branches work in tandem. Cogs in a machine for the better. They don't compete for power, they have unique functions that keep the power divided but cohesive"

"Hey Finn, I'm still getting through your paper here and sure glad I'm not the one who has to write it. How about adding some acknowledgement of Wardens' terms to it? I might be a machines guy, but you'll definitely find in me an ally of keeping harmony and balance with nature and people beyond our homes. I don't suppose anyone here is setting their sights on conquest or disrupting this balance, might as well guarantee it as our responsibility to the land we want to call our home."
"Nature is something we cannot and should not seek to control."
"A treaty shouldn't be written into a constitution. Those documents are separate things."
"Not the whole thing. Acknowledgement of our responsibility towards this land where we make our homes. Isn't this constitution something to be a foundation of the nation?"

"Hmm what would you have in mind with it? Our responsibility to take care of the land? I'll admit it does seem a bit out of the scope of what a constitution may hold, but I won't say it couldn't be added or changed to make sense somewhere"

she nods. 'Nature is more powerful than any of us. If we disrespect it, our descendants will be the ones paying the price.'
"It's an important responsibility."

Ryan Kelly nods, before waving off his wife, who was looking concerned in his direction. "Of course, of course. I only meant that it's hard to... to find you in a crowd when you don't ahhh... look quite like a person." He nods once more and walks off.
an imp follows them, `Surely it's easier to find someone in a crowd when they look different from the majority?`
